text:
Maya R: Heads-up: seeing a persistent p99 spike (~4.2s) on the hosted route since 03:10 UTC. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms, p99 jumps for ~0.7% of requests. Only affects models on v2-kernels. Anyone seeing this in profiling?

Kevin L: saw the alert. grabbing traces now. initial thought: kernel selection fallback to generic CUDA kernel for long sequences? :thinking_face:

perf-bot: perf-regression detected: service=runtime route=/v2/generate p99 +1.8s vs baseline. linked traces: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1753205432

Sanjay P: quick datapoint: distribution shows a small tail of requests with input token counts > 1500. that pushes sequence length up and forces different attention kernels. microbatch_size also increased temporarily to 16 during the window (we had a burst).

Olivia C: KV cache stats from the same window: global kv_miss_rate spiked from 1.2% -> 9.4%. lots of rekey events logged (tool-call context switching). when a request does a tool call we append long tool metadata which looks like new prompt prefixes. cache uniqueness explodes.

Maya R: minimal repro in staging: send a long prompt (~2k tokens) that triggers a tool-call loop (model emits tool call -> app responds -> model continues). p99 high and tail very long. Posting trace snippet: 

```
[TRACE] request_id=abc123
step=token_generate duration=0.38s kernel=fast_attn
step=tool_call_start duration=0.02s
step=tool_response_append size=1800 tokens
step=token_generate duration=2.15s kernel=fallback_gemm  <-- big jump
step=token_generate duration=1.05s kernel=fallback_gemm
```

Maya R: note kernel switched mid-request once seq_len > 1024, and fallback_gemm is ~5x slower on our A100 tuning for this config.

Kevin L: confirmed. kernel selector picks fast_attn for seq<=1024 and fallback_gemm otherwise. problem is we let microbatching combine short and long requests. larger microbatch means the long seq forces selection for whole batch on some code paths.

Sanjay P: exact. scheduler uses per-microbatch max_seq to select kernels. with microbatch_size=16 a single long prompt in batch forces the batch kernel to fallback. that explains p95 stable but p99 blowup.

Olivia C: tool-call loops worse: each tool response appends tokens and often includes JSON blobs. KV cache keys use prompt prefix fingerprint; when tool responses differ we get misses and cold KV loads. combined effect: extra decode work + cache misses -> compounded tail.

Logan M: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enforce per-request fast-path cutoff: if seq_len > 1024 route to isolated microbatch (size=1) / different queue; 2) clamp microbatch_size when mixture of seq lengths detected; 3) create a separate tool-call routing pipeline that uses robust quantized kernels.

Kevin L: experimented in dev: clamp microbatch to 4 for mixed-length queue reduces p99 from 4.2s -> 760ms on the noisy cohort. still some overhead from KV misses but big win.

Maya R: can we add heuristic: if request has tool call markers or expected interactive tool loop, tag as high-variance and route to conservative queue?

Olivia C: yes, we already detect tool_call tokens in preproc. adding a route flag is trivial in router. KV eviction policy also needs work: we should avoid rekeying on trivially different tool response ids, maybe normalize templates.

Sanjay P: another angle: kernel selector could consider per-sample kernel instead of batch-global if we can afford scatter-gather at op level. expensive to implement but would eliminate batch-level fallback. worth exploring as longer-term.

Logan M: short-term plan proposed: (A) clamp microbatch to 4 for mixed queues (canary today), (B) add route flag for tool-call heavy requests -> isolated queue, (C) normalize tool-call payloads before computing KV key to reduce miss churn.

Maya R: going to run canary on a subset (10% traffic) with microbatch clamp + tool flag. posting canary config here: 

```
# runtime canary
route_match: "model:*-v2-kernel && region:us-east"
queue_policy:
  mixed_length_microbatch: clamp_to: 4
  tool_call_isolation: true
p95_target_ms: "300"
p99_target_ms: "800"
```

Kevin L: also adding extra tracing for per-token kernel decisions and kv_hit boolean. want to capture whether kernel flip correlates with KV miss.

perf-bot: canary launched for route=/v2/generate (10%) at 1753205600.

Olivia C: one more note: quantized kernels are less sensitive to sequence length on our hardware; we could recommend the quantized variant for tool-heavy workloads as a config-level suggestion in Optimize.

Sanjay P: filed follow-ups: GH-#4122 (kernel selector per-sample prototype), GH-#4123 (kv normalization), GH-#4124 (router flags + canary).

Maya R: thanks everyone. will monitor canary and report back in 30m. if p99 still bad we'll consider emergency rate-limit on long prompts as fallback. :eyes: 

Logan M: ping me if you want me to flip the canary to 25% after initial green.

Kevin L: notes for postmortem: root causes = (1) batch-level kernel selection + mixed-length microbatching, (2) KV cache churn due to tool-call payload variance, (3) outlier long prompts that trigger fallback kernel. mitigations: microbatch clamping, routing flag, kv normalization, longer-term per-sample kernel scheduling.

Maya R: update 30m: canary p99 down to 680ms, kv_miss_rate reduced to 2.1%. leaving canary at 10% while we validate logs. will open a short postmortem draft after stabilizing.

Olivia C: nice. can add a dashboard tile for tool-call tail percentage so we catch this earlier.

perf-bot: alert resolved for now.

Maya R: closing thread once postmortem link is up. great work all. :tada:
